QF.id: VI Public Offering and Corporate Actions_15

question.text: In case of a rights issue of a listed company, in which ISIN are the rights shares credited upon allotment?

answer.text: A new temporary ISIN which is frozen for debit
The existing ISIN of the company
The ISIN of the Rights Entitlements

explanation.text: The Logic: Rights shares are credited in a new (temporary) ISIN of the company that is frozen for debit, so the securities cannot be transferred until they are available for trading. The Trap: The existing ISIN may seem intuitive, but a temporary ISIN is used to prevent any trading before the rights shares are listed. Note: The temporary ISIN ensures that no trading occurs before the rights shares are listed for trading.
